{"self_assessment": "Impact: Early on I spotted that the start sat in the tail notch while the body lines began to its left, so the fall would never have reached them. I flagged it and suggested moving the start to the nose and branching from there, and the table redrew around that. Without that fix the push would not have reached the fish body. I also laid the lower fork tip, which completed the tail that makes the outline read as a fish. Before the push, the chain traced by eye from the nose through all 111 standing dominoes.

Execution: I put my hands on the fiddly parts: the crossing at the tail neck and the lower join. I laid the dominoes extending past the crossing, stood one back up, and nudged an off-line domino into line at the lower join. I inspected the crossing and join twice, at 4:30 and 5:00, and confirmed the fall passed through. I then kept my hands off the crossing so I wouldn't risk a bump close to the push.

Collaboration: I backed Tom's idea of splitting the long runs, offered to take the top run, and coordinated hand positions so we stayed clear of each other. I took the tail work and stayed out of the others' areas. When Maya preferred not to redraw the pad, I accepted that and adjusted by helping where the lines were behind.

Leadership: I took the tail and the join checks without being asked and reported what I found to the table in plain terms. I called for hands-off once the fish was connected, which helped keep the finished crossing intact for the push.", "my_share_percent": 25}
